messages.text:
Next: 

Based on the experience with the pixel detector, develop a similar detailed model for the short strips, start with the barrel:

- realistic model placement
- local support and mounting
- necessary cabling and cooling
- cable and cooling routing
I’ll review the short-strip design records and the pixel model’s placement, support and service approach, then develop a detailed barrel proposal with traceable inputs and validation.

The short-strip study already fixes a 75 µm × 0.5 mm strixel baseline. I’ll keep that and develop the barrel as an isolated prototype with tangential/longitudinal sensor axes, staggered modules, shared cooling staves and explicit service routes. The readout hardware is still unresolved, so I’ll show the service load assumptions and any failures alongside the geometry.

I’m using the acts-spack skill to verify the local DD4hep/Geant4 runtime before native validation.

The Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints. I’ll verify the installed runtime directly before using it.

The existing study also shows a major services uncertainty: each proposed strixel module has 122,880 channels. I’ll retain both the CMS power comparator and the larger channel-scaled stress case, with separate checks for local cooling and collected cable capacity.

DD4hep 1.38, ROOT 6.40.04 and Geant4 11.4.2 import successfully; the Geant4 datasets are present.

For the barrel, I’m developing straight, serviceable staves with alternating radial module heights to cover axial seams. Short thermal pickups will connect the raised modules to the common cold structure while clearing neighbouring modules. Each half-stave will have its own cooling loop and service termination at the corresponding barrel end.

The draft now has sensor and readout layers, thermal pickups, cooling tubes and coolant, buses, bearing rings, mounting feet and service-sector inventories.

One routing check already fails: the inherited 30 mm collector depth is too shallow for the proposed finished cables with 25–50 mm bend allowances. I’ll keep that failure visible; a volume-normalized service cell cannot demonstrate that the bends fit.

The first compact export correctly rejected the 30 mm collector: its cable inventory exceeded the available volume. I’m retaining that failed case and proposing a 65 mm collector. That fits the larger bend allowance, but requires review of the first short-strip endcap position.

I’ve also reduced the trial row lift to 1.5 mm, consistent with the roughly 1 mm module stack, and the stave-lane spacing to 12 mm. Native clearance and coverage checks will test those choices.

The first coverage sample found that a 2 mm azimuthal margin leaves gaps for 1 GeV tracks in a 4 T field: bending shifts the crossing point between the staggered radial lanes. I’m testing an 8 mm margin and retaining the original result.

I’m also diagnosing a native factory crash. No native validation pass has been recorded yet.

I found the crash: naming the factory function `create` caused it to recurse inside DD4hep’s registration macro. That’s corrected, and native validation is running again.

The 8 mm margin reduces the coverage misses. The current sample still has barrel-end misses against the original nominal-cylinder boundaries; I’ll quantify those separately from interior seams so the later endcap study has a clear acceptance target.

The revised native geometry passes: **7,952 sensitive modules, zero overlaps at 10⁻⁵ mm**, matching transforms and material inventories, and successful identifier checks. The overlap audit caught flex tails passing through the stave core; they now wrap around its outside edge.

The engineering screens remain conditional. The lower power comparator passes the cold thermal screen, while the channel-scaled load fails. Conservative and channel-scaled cable-demand cases also exceed the fixed corridor.

The dense coverage check is complete: 103,040 trajectories per charge mode over |η|≤4 and five luminous-region positions. It found no misses more than 100 mm from a nominal barrel end; the remaining misses are recorded against the original boundary.

The services model now includes data-link demand as well as power. The inherited cable and fibre sizes remain benchmarks: several load scenarios need more links or routing space, so they cannot yet define a qualified electronics package.

The transverse Geant4 smoke test succeeded and recorded hits in all four barrel layers. The model now includes the staves, mounting rings, cooling loops, module flexes and end-service routes.

The checks also exposed a real interface problem: the collector needs more space and conflicts with the old first endcap-disc position. I’m recording that, along with the power and bandwidth limits, in the draft design and validation report.

I recommend keeping the straight staves with tangential/axial sensor axes and independent cooling loops for each half. That gives clear assembly datums and accessible connections at both barrel ends.

The draft records 7,952 modules and preserves the failed engineering screens. The next decisions are the readout package and the collector/endcap interface: the current power, cable and bandwidth benchmarks cannot yet define buildable hardware.

The draft drawings and report are ready. The native overlap check is clean, and the saved Geant4 event confirms sensitive hits. The coverage sample still shows losses near the nominal barrel ends, so those remain a failed boundary check.

I’m finishing the review package and session journal, then publishing a draft PR with the remaining mechanical and service decisions listed explicitly.

[Draft PR #49](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/49) is published with both drawings, the detailed model and validation evidence. Hosted checks are running.

The PR keeps the remaining decisions visible: readout feasibility, collector/endcap clearance, real cable and manifold routing, and finite-area mounting seats. The session journal also validates; this active turn’s token counters remain unavailable.

The hosted run has passed the shared geometry checks and moved on to the remaining controls. I’m waiting for its result before closing the review record.

The report’s main next-step recommendation is to settle the readout and service interfaces before subsystem integration: power and bandwidth can change the routing requirement substantially.
The new short-strip controls have now passed on GitHub. The remaining checks cover the dashboard and publication metadata. The standalone DD4hep and Geant4 results are already retained in the PR.

Hosted validation passed on the scientific model commit. The PR contains the full design, drawings, reproducible commands and retained failed attempts.

I’m publishing the final tracking and journal update. The model is ready for review; the engineering gates remain open.

Created [draft PR #49](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/49) with the detailed short-strip barrel model:

- Four layers, **284 staves and 7,952 modules**, with tangential/axial sensor axes.
- Carbon sandwich supports, thermal pickups, mounting rings and feet.
- Independent half-stave CO₂ cooling loops, insulated buses, flexes and end boards.
- Module-to-sector cable and cooling routes.

DD4hep construction passed with **zero overlaps**; Geant4 recorded hits in all four layers. Hosted model checks passed; the final journal/tracking update’s CI is running.

The [design and validation report]([redacted] identifies the remaining work: collector/endcap clearance, finite-area mounting seats, barrel-end coverage losses, and readout/thermal/service qualification. The design remains DRAFT.

Session logging is retained; this active turn’s token counters remain unknown.
